The *Sūcidāyakattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative located in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Khuddakanikāya [SuttaCentral]. It forms part of the late canonical biographical literature celebrating the past karmic deeds and gifts of early Buddhist elders. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages, though it does not document any curated external parallels [SuttaCentral].
Computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 18 Pali-internal matches across four texts, illustrating the formulaic and conventional nature of verse composition within the Apadāna and commentary traditions [DharmaNexus]. The text shares extended passages with the first volume of the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, segment ranges §4.2–5.3 aligned with §1513–1516) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits significant formulaic overlap with other poems in the Therāpadāna, including an identically named apadāna (*Sūcidāyakattheraapadāna*, Tha-Ap 96; §5.3–8.1 completely identical to §4.2–7.1), the *Ādhāradāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 211; §4.1–8.1 aligned with §2.1–6.1), and the *Pallaṅkadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 152; §5.3–7.1 aligned with §4.2–6.1) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus notes minor similarities with Kṣemendra's Sanskrit *Sumāgadhāvadāna* (best plausibility score 25), though these reflect shared conventional verse fragments rather than established recensional parallels [DharmaNexus].
